subject.title: [Feature]: Recover the in-flight gateway run on CLI disconnect (reattach-first) instead of recook-first embedded fallback

question: Should accepted non-transient gateway disconnects reattach to the authoritative run before any embedded fallback, and should that policy apply uniformly or differ between interactive stdout and `--deliver`?
rationale: This is a user-visible compatibility tradeoff involving streaming, result authority, duplicated side effects, and delivery behavior; source inspection alone cannot select the intended product contract.

options.title: Adopt reattach-first
options.body: Make the accepted gateway run authoritative, wait and replay its terminal result, then use the existing isolated fallback only after recovery becomes unknown or expires.

options.title: Keep recook-first
options.body: Retain immediate embedded fallback for all modes, accepting rare duplicate execution in exchange for predictable local streaming and prompt stdout behavior.

options.title: Split by delivery mode
options.body: Use reattach-first for `--deliver` while retaining recook-first for interactive stdout until a stronger interactive recovery UX is designed.

recommendation.title: Adopt reattach-first
recommendation.body: Make the accepted gateway run authoritative, wait and replay its terminal result, then use the existing isolated fallback only after recovery becomes unknown or expires.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline shows direct involvement after the full recovery proposal was linked, and the remaining blocker is product direction rather than a narrow mechanical repair.
